Distance = Speed × Time

⇒200 + x = 450

= 27 × (5)/(18) m/s

= 7.5 m/s

= Distance/ Speed (Here distance is the length of the train and speed = relative speed)

= (250)/(15+7.5)

= (250)/(22.5)

= 11.1 seconds

**Hence, The time taken by the train to pass the man is 11.1 seconds.**

questions.question: Raja borrowed Rs. 15,000 on simple interest at the rate of 13% per annum and lent it on compound interest at the rate of 15% per annum, compounded annually. What is Raja's gain in two years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total **Simple Interest** rate for 2 years = 13% × 2 = 26%

Effective **Compound Interest** rate for 2 years = 15 + 15 + (15 × 15)/100 = 32.25%

Net **Gain percentage** = 32.25% − 26% = 6.25%

Raja's **Total Gain** = 6.25% of ₹15,000 = 150 × 6.25 = ₹937.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹937.50.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (**P**) = ₹15,000

Simple Interest rate (**R₁**) = 13% p.a.

Compound Interest rate (**R₂**) = 15% p.a.

Time period (**T**) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (**SI**) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Compound Interest (**CI**) = P × [(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94ef34b88da64d92f43234b3c06c1b1441703fdbc7f0e962f2a3fc644e58cb6d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = (15,000 × 13 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 150 × 26 = ₹3,900

⇒ **Compound Interest (CI)** Amount = 15,000 × (1 + 15/100)²

⇒ CI Amount = 15,000 × (1.15) × (1.15) = 15,000 × 1.3225 = ₹19,837.50

⇒ CI = ₹19,837.50 − ₹15,000 = ₹4,837.50

⇒ **Raja's Gain** = CI − SI = 4,837.50 − 3,900 = ₹937.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹937.50.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effective Percentage Rate for CI

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate is calculated using the successive percentage formula: x + y + (xy/100).

Difference between CI and SI

When the rate (R) is the same for both, the difference for 2 years is P(R/100)². Here, rates were different, so we calculate each separately.

Compounding Annually

In annual compounding, the interest for the first year is added to the principal to calculate the interest for the second year.
